import os, re
from collections import defaultdict

root = '/bench/repo'
internal = os.path.join(root, 'internal')

# Extract function/method declarations
func_re = re.compile(r'^func\s+(?:\(([^)]+)\)\s+)?(\w+)\s*\(', re.MULTILINE)

decls = []  # (name, recv, path, package)

for dirpath, _, files in os.walk(internal):

        path = os.path.join(dirpath, f)

print(f'Non-test: {sum(1 for d in decls if not d[4])}')

value.text:
A Perl script bug caused an "Odd number of elements in anonymous hash" error. The `is_method` flag was set to `$recv ne ""`, which produced an empty value when the receiver string was empty.

The actual cause of the hash error is the `exported` flag. Its regex `($name =~ /^[A-Z]/)` returns an empty list when no match occurs, producing an odd number of hash elements. The method call counts are also unreliable; generic patterns like `.Len(` and `.Next(` are matching too broadly across unrelated symbols.

Package-level results look more reliable than method counts. `util.GenUUID` shows 28 calls across 9 files, which seems plausible. `filter.NewEngine` shows 32 calls across only 4 files, suggesting possible overcounting from declarations or test files. `ConvertStringToInt32` at only 5 calls looks suspicious, likely due to import alias detection errors. Some high-fan-in functions may have been missed because of import path mismatches.

The `NewEngine` overcount likely stems from same-package regex matches and `DefaultEngine` callers. Interface methods and comment occurrences may also be inflating totals. `GenUUID`, `ConvertStringToInt32`, `HasPrefixes`, and `ValidateEmail` still need closer verification.

Exact grep checks will isolate the true top call sites. `profile.AllowAnonymous` is another candidate. The regex pattern appears to match inside comments, which explains why `NewEngine` registers 32 callers despite being a single declaration.

The same-package regex is correctly scoped to internal files, so the 32 NewEngine calls are not caused by cross-package overcounting. The next step is to grep exact call sites for the top candidates. Methods such as CompileToStatement, AllowAnonymous, ExtractTags, and ConvertStringToInt32 should also be examined.

`CompileToStatement` has 38 calls across 9 files. This is a genuine high-fan-in result. `addArg` has 28 calls within a single file. These method counts appear valid. `SortVersion.Len` and `Schedule.Next` remain false positives from broad regex matches.

The same-package regex likely inflates `NewEngine` counts. `CompileToStatement` still needs verification. `GenUUID`, `HasPrefixes`, and `ConvertStringToInt32` also need closer inspection. Import alias detection probably failed for `ConvertStringToInt32`. Test files should count toward fan-in.

Common interface methods such as ExtractTags and RenderHTML are now being checked for high call counts. Thorough greps will verify these candidates.
The first pass inflated common method names, so I’ll verify unique symbols and recount their real call sites.

Reconsidering whether test functions should count as callers. NewEngine may have roughly 32 distinct callers if all ~30 test functions are included. GenUUID has about 6 to 7 production callers.

addArg appears to have roughly 15 to 20 distinct callers within its own file alone. If test functions are counted as callers, GenUUID could reach approximately 27 total callers.

Evaluating whether to include test functions in the inbound-call count. If tests are counted, CompileToStatement likely leads with roughly 38 callers, while NewEngine reaches about 32. Excluding tests, addArg appears to have the highest inbound fan-in at approximately 28 distinct callers. The "approx" qualifier allows rounding to these rough figures.

Checking whether any function under internal/ exceeds CompileToStatement’s roughly 38 callers. Interface methods like isCondition and goldmark Kind() are unlikely to be direct callers. Functions inside test files under internal/ may have been overlooked.

Test helpers declared under internal/ are explicitly included by the question. Now checking whether interface methods on markdown.Service, such as ExtractTags or RenderHTML, contribute to the inbound-call count.

# Cross-package inbound for all unique exported internal funcs
# Count only calls from outside the declaring package

echo "=== Exported unique symbols: cross-package call sites ==="

# Get exported func names from internal non-test
find /bench/repo/internal -name '*.go' ! -name '*_test.go' | while read f; do
  pkg=$(grep -m1 '^package ' "$f" | awk '{print $2}')
  grep -E '^func [A-Z]' "$f" | sed -E 's/^func ([A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*).*/\1/' | while read name; do
    echo "$name	$pkg	$f"
  done
  grep -E '^func \([^)]+\) [A-Z]' "$f" | sed -E 's/^func \([^)]+\) ([A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*).*/\1/' | while read name; do
    echo "$name	$pkg	$f"
  done
done > /tmp/exported.txt

# For each unique exported name, count calls outside declaring package
sort -u /tmp/exported.txt | while IFS=$'\t' read name pkg path; do
  # skip common names that collide
  case "$name" in New|Validate|Send|Render|Parse|Start|Stop|Format|Field|Compile|Len|Next|Register) continue ;; esac
  
  # count call lines not in files of that package
  count=$(grep -rn --include='*.go' -E "(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])${name}[[:space:]]*\(" /bench/repo \
    --exclude-dir=web --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=proto 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -v ':func ' \
    | grep -v "${name} converts\|${name} returns\|${name} builds\|${name} reports\|${name} compiles" \
    | while IFS=: read file line rest; do
        fpkg=$(grep -m1 '^package ' "$file" | awk '{print $2}')
        if [ "$fpkg" != "$pkg" ]; then
          echo "$file"
        fi
      done | wc -l)
  if [ "$count" -gt 2 ]; then
    echo "$count	$name	$pkg	$path"
  fi
done | sort -n
